title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 30 | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Jeremiyah Love is expected to play Sunday after two weeks out, while Hjalte Froholdt is limited with a tweak and Hayden Conner would step in at center.
summary: LaFleur said the running game has improved since the muddy-field games, but it is still a work in progress and depends on building continuity among the mix of backs and linemen. He expects Jeremiyah Love to play Sunday and said Love will be good, though no player is at 100% this early in the season. Elijah Wilkinson is healthy enough to be full on Friday despite a rib issue that is a pain-tolerance matter. Hjalte Froholdt is limited after a tweak suffered Thursday, and the staff will reassess him Friday and Saturday. If Froholdt can't go, Hayden Conner would move into the middle. LaFleur said the staff prepares for every lineup scenario. He also described Will Johnson as having a strong demeanor and an edge in practice, and said he is positioned to play if called upon. LaFleur said he expects the recently added veteran receiver to be fully involved, though he is working with the scout team and needs more time with the first-team offense. In the red zone discussion, LaFleur said points and wins are what matter, and that the offense has to finish drives starting with him. He also gave a thoughtful answer on how the market devalues linebackers and said he thinks the position is beginning to rise again.

title: Jesse Minter Announces Lamar Jackson's Return
headline: Lamar Jackson is expected to return and play against the Bills, with the coach saying he looked full in all three practices this week.
summary: Coach Jesse Minter opened by saying the team is excited for a chance to play a strong opponent in a difficult environment, and he praised the week of preparation. He said the team expects Lamar Jackson to play this week after a good week of practice, and he believes Jackson was full in all three practice days. Minter credited Jackson for working through an injury to get back on the field. He said Jackson will look like himself and play his usual style of football, and he dismissed the idea that Jackson would be a passive or 'statue' presence. Minter also said Jackson's return will give the team a boost. He praised the backup quarterback for keeping the team in position to win the last three games, but he emphasized that the team does not need to lean on Jackson alone. On G Olaivavega Ioane, Minter said Ioane has worked hard to try to be available, but the final decision will come in the next couple of hours and the injury report will show it. Minter said Jaylinn Hawkins will be out this week.

title: Joe Brady Addresses Bills Injury Updates, Starting Safety, And Challenges In Facing The Baltimore Ravens
headline: Damar Hamlin gets the starting safety job Sunday vs. Baltimore, and several starters (Kincaid, DJ Moore, Spencer Brown, Dee Alford) are questionable with lower-body issues.
summary: Brady opened with the injury report: Dalton Kincaid, DJ Moore, Spencer Brown, and Dee Alford are questionable, Greg Gaines is also listed as questionable, and Tyrell Shavers is out. He said the group tweaked a lower-body issue in practice. On Spencer Brown, Brady said he trusts the left tackle's preparation and experience to perform even without many practice reps, so he expects him to be able to play. Brady said no one is fully healthy this late in the season and that Baltimore will present the best version of Lamar Jackson. He praised three strong practice days after the bye and the team's attention to detail. Damar Hamlin will start at safety, and Brady said the team has several options at nickel and will use versatile players to cover different fits. On Baltimore's defense, Brady said new coordinator Jesse Minter has adjusted the scheme from his Chargers and Michigan stops, and that the Bills must prepare for new wrinkles and a different look from Baltimore's past defenses. Brady said self-scouting led to focused improvement without losing the defense's identity. He also flagged Zay Flowers as a major challenge who can line up inside or outside and has strong chemistry with Jackson. Brady closed by saying Hamlin has earned the start, handles multiple positions, and will make the most of the extra snaps.

title: Dave Canales addresses defensive coaching changes
headline: Canales overhauls the defensive staff with Todd Walsh as interim coordinator; Will Lee's hamstring timeline is pending, and the offense is being asked to balance its vertical passing with quicker concepts.
summary: Dave Canales said the defensive coordinator change was his decision, made after gathering information over time and weighing the schedule, the team's divisional position, and the need to get the most from the roster. He framed the move as laying groundwork for the style of football he wants, with the run game and winning first and second down as the foundation. Todd Walsh takes over as interim coordinator, and Canales praised his experience, his connection with players, and his scheme knowledge. Renaldo Hill will take over the secondary, and A.C. Carter moves to coach the front and defensive tackles, freeing Walsh for more coordinator duties. Canales said the locker room reaction is still being gauged and that staff staffing is being discussed through the weekend. On offense, he acknowledged that the vertical passing game has run into protection problems and that opponents are starting to attack it, so the staff wants more balance through quicker, shallower concepts. He said the offensive line is being reevaluated each week and that Brady Christensen is "doing great" and is one possibility for the lineup. He also said the extra days before Monday will be used to regroup ahead of the Broncos game.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury; Canales said a clearer timeline will come shortly after evaluation and would not say whether he is an IR candidate.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference - October 30th, 2026
headline: Michael Hall is back in the rotation for the Steelers game, while Tytus Howard's status remains unresolved until Saturday morning.
summary: Monken said the staff will have a clearer read on Tytus Howard in the morning, with another practice Saturday to work through it, and that Howard's performance in practice has been fine. He said Michael Hall tried to play last week but could not, and that Hall's return is a real boost to a defensive line that has depth thanks to the elevated player who filled in up front. Monken said Hall's disruption will help fix the fit problems that let Tennessee run the ball, and he praised Hall for returning to finish a prior game after being knocked out. On Jared Verse's comments calling Pittsburgh dirty, Monken said he had not seen them, has great respect for the Steelers' physical style, and expects a loud environment because CLE is playing better. He credited the offense's improvement against Tennessee to collective effort in protection, ball distribution, and staying ahead of the chains rather than any single player. Monken said the team's mindset is to move on quickly from mistakes, taking things one play at a time. He said he has not yet decided on the backup quarterback plan for the Pittsburgh game and will designate one of four options later.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 10-30-26
headline: Coach Schottenheimer says DeMarvion Overshown is back and Tyler Smith is playing well, with Dak Prescott's trust and the run-heavy approach both reaffirmed ahead of Week 8 at Arizona.
summary: Schottenheimer said his team is balancing run and pass, and that the commitment to the run came after struggles against Tampa Bay and Green Bay. He credited a much-improved offensive line, with Tyler Smith back for his third week and playing well, for the physical run game against Philadelphia. He described protection improvements as a function of the group playing together more, and said defenses are using twists and stunts to stress protections. He defended Dak Prescott's awareness on the late-game run call that kept the Cowboys' field position in mind, and said he has more confidence in Prescott than anyone. On defense he said health is the big driver, with bodies returning, and singled out Joey Porter Jr., Shemar James, and Quinnen Williams as playing well. He previewed Arizona by praising Budda Baker and Trey McBride and noting the Cardinals' multi-safety looks, and said the Cowboys have struggled against them recently and need to take care of the ball.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “The Ball Is What This Game Comes Down To” | Press Conference
headline: Shemar James has locked in as the Cowboys' middle linebacker, while Dee Winters is likely out another week and Luke Schoonmaker is a late-week check.
summary: Schottenheimer said Shemar James has earned the middle linebacker job, praising his command and calming influence on the defense. He described the linebacker spot as a rotation by nature, with Jaishawn Barham and DeMarvion Overshown cross-trained and playing different packages based on formation and call. He said Dee Winters will be hard to get back this week and is probably a week away. He called Pickens, Quinnen Williams and Caleb Downs healthy enough to play, and said Luke Schoonmaker is fine but he wants to see how he moves at practice. On Arizona, he said turnovers, not energy, are the reason the Cowboys have lost four straight at home, pointing to an 11-turnover deficit in those games. He said the defense is ready for Arizona's disguised blitzes, and that the offense must get Trey McBride boxed in because the ball will go his way. He credited the offensive line and tight ends for consistent run blocking and gave game balls to the line, including Broderick Jones. He also said a roster decision would come after practice.

summary: Payton said the Broncos have a deep running back room with three backs, which makes balancing the rotation harder than with two. He said Dobbins is doing well, that his production has peaked, and that analytics on burst and speed support the depth. Asked about RJ Harvey, he said there was no status update. He described target planning for receivers and tight ends as more fixed than running back touches, which can shift with the flow of a game. On red-zone defense, he credited stopping the run and getting off the field on third down. He explained that jumbo personnel is game-dependent and sometimes used to force the base defense into a look the team wants to run, with Trautman and Engram as examples. He framed the Chiefs game as a divisional matchup that matters and said the team does not break the season into quarters. Against Seattle's run game, he said pursuit to the ball was the main emphasis.

title: Campbell on Minnesota Vikings
headline: Kerby Joseph has no limitations for the Vikings game after playing every defensive rep in the second half; Gibbs praised as a complete back; Pacheco still rehabbing toward a possible mid-December return.
summary: Campbell said Kerby Joseph has progressed well through individual and group work, with team reps still to come, and that he will be in full practice next week. He dismissed the sleeve Joseph wore as a routine swelling precaution. After a conservative first half, Joseph played nearly every defensive rep in the second half, and Campbell said there are no limitations on him for this game. Campbell praised Jahmyr Gibbs as a complete back who takes pride in running, receiving, pass protection and physicality. On Vikings edge rusher Dallas Turner, Campbell called him a rising, difficult threat who is hard for tackles to handle one-on-one. He said Cade Mays took more reps than Brian Branch in practice and should benefit from a second week back. On the injury front, Isiah Pacheco is progressing well with a chance to return in mid-to-late December, and Devin White is also doing pretty well. Thomas Harper is close to being ready and is being held as a precaution. Campbell said the division matchup matters, with Minnesota 2-0 in the NFC North, and that the team must play cleaner football, while trade-deadline activity continues daily.

title: Matt LaFleur likes 'the aggressive style' defense showed against Panthers
headline: Christian Watson returned to the game after a precautionary CT scan, and Ty'Ron Hopper had a big game, but the run game remains a major concern.
summary: LaFleur praised the defense for holding a Carolina offense with a lot of explosive plays, especially in the second half when the offense struggled. He said the team handled its injury problems by having players step up, and he highlighted John Williams playing center for the second time and Ty'Ron Hopper's multi-takeaway game. He explained the offensive line shuffle as keeping Larkin in the lineup while Aaron Banks returned, and said Zeitler moved to right guard, a spot he had rarely practiced. On the closing drive he called the run game going backwards disappointing and said he had seen little reason for optimism there. He described Christian Watson's collapse-and-return as a precautionary situation that he cleared before going back in. LaFleur credited Jordan Love for carrying the offense despite the interception, and he praised Jonathan Gannon's aggressive, pressure-heavy defensive scheme. He also defended keeping Coleman Owen after his opening-kickoff fumble, saying he had done a good job since.

title: Liam Coen Reviews Strong Week of Practice, Talks Game Plan for Colts | Press Conference

He also said he has not game-planned for Thursday night yet, as he prefers to focus on the current opponent.

He called the NFC North the best division in football and noted a tough upcoming stretch including a Monday night game and a trip to Lambeau. Finally, he credited Myles Price's development as a returner, citing his kick returns and a punt return that flipped the field, and called Price a huge part of the team's success this year.

summary: Bowles addressed an unnamed player's foot injury, which is the main fantasy-relevant item. title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Carnell Tate (shoulder) sat Friday with his game status uncertain, while Alontae Taylor is nearing a return and competing with Marcus Harris for the nickel job.
summary: Saleh opened by saying Carnell Tate, who was listed as "Taj" in the captions, and a second player whose name was garbled, would not practice Friday, and that their game status was in doubt until after the workout. He said the team would push Tate in a limited workout to see how the shoulder responds, and called the situation complicated for a young player. Saleh believes Tate hurt the shoulder on a fumble and that players often don't feel injuries until the next morning. On the defense, he said blitz usage is decided game by game, not because of a lost pass rusher, and that the team is weighing packages with two corners, nickel, dime, or even a three-defensive-lineman look, since Jeff's absence is a factor. Alontae Taylor had a strong week, especially in pads, and is getting closer to playing. Saleh described nickel as a linebacker-like role and said Taylor still has to take the job from Marcus Harris, who has played well. Saleh said Taylor's extra snaps last week reflected earned reps and improved communication. On Cam Ward being the franchise face, Saleh said that is a natural expectation for any quarterback but that the focus is on Ward's daily development. Saleh closed by celebrating a high school coach of the week.
